Be sure to join out FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com! The Boston Red Sox made a massive gamble ahead of the trade deadline, sending a massive haul of prospects to the Baltimore Orioles in exchange for three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. After underperforming in 32 games with Boston, Rutschman now enters his final yea
item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses the calculus the Red Sox have to make when considering a potential contract extension for All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. Be sure to join out FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
The Boston Red Sox made a massive gamble ahead of the trade deadline, sending a massive haul of prospects to the Baltimore Orioles in exchange for three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. After underperforming in 32 games with Boston, Rutschman now enters his final year of salary arbitration. But the Red Sox face a tough decision on whether to try to extend Rutschman ahead of the 2027 season.
Here's what a potential extension could look like:
What is Rutschman looking for?
Prior to being traded to Boston, Rutschman had exploratory talks with Baltimore about a potential extension. "Rutschman, then, would probably want a deal that makes him a lifetime Oriole, or close to it," wrote The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal on July 6. "His benchmark might be the nine-year, $167 million extension Buster Posey signed with the San Francisco Giants in March 2013," he continued.
The idea that Rutschman could be in line for a deal like Posey's, who will almost assuredly be in Cooperstown in the near future, is a bit far-fetched. Prior to signing that deal, Posey posted a career slash line of .314/.380/.503/.883 with 46 home runs and 191 RBI, winning the 2010 National League Rookie of the Year award, the 2012 National League Most Valuable Player award, and two World Series titles. A far cry from Rutschman's .252/.339/.414/.753 with 74 home runs and 290 RBI, with a career accolade list of three All-Star appearances.
Catchers typically struggle to capitalize on their value given the high injury risk from the wear and tear of being behind the plate nightly. Rutschman is no stranger to those concerns, having played just 189 games over the last two seasons.
Beyond Rutschman's worse resume than Posey's, the Red Sox have shied away from deals that take players well into their 30s, with the longest deal in recent memory being the eight-year extension given to Roman Anthony, which takes him through his age-29 season.
Comparisons
With Posey's nine-year deal seemingly out the window, we'll have to look at some more recent catcher deals, which… gets complicated, to say the least. Of the five richest deals signed by catchers, only one was signed with one year of service time remaining: Toronto Blue Jays' Alejandro Kirk. So let's start there:
Kirk
Ahead of the 2026 season, Kirk signed a five-year, $58-million deal to remain in Toronto through 2030. Before signing, Kirk was a two-time All-Star with a career line of .268/.345/.398/.743. Like Rutschman, Kirk is a strong defensive catcher when it comes to blocking balls in the dirt and framing. However, he struggles to throw runners out.
Though an average annual value of $11.6 million feels low based on Rosenthal's reporting, we'll have to keep looking.
Sean Murphy
At 29, Murphy signed a six-year, $73-million extension with the Atlanta Braves, buying out his final two years of arbitration. According to Spotrac, Murphy was paid $9 million in 2024, his penultimate arbitration year, and $15 million annually for the remainder of the deal.
At the time of signing, Murphy posted a .240/.336/.441/.778 line with 67 home runs and 215 RBI, earning an All-Star selection and becoming one of the game's best defensive catchers.
Cal Raleigh
The runner-up for the 2025 American League Most Valuable Player award, Raleigh signed a six-year, $105-million deal to remain with the Seattle Mariners through the 2030 season, buying out his final three arbitration years. In the four seasons leading up to his extension, Raleigh posted a line of .218/.296/.444/.740 with 93 home runs and 251 RBI. Defensively. Raleigh is a mixed bag, with improving blocking skills, but is middle of the road in both framing and throwing runners out.
Raleigh's deal is also slightly different than the one Rutschman would be looking to sign. While his deal carries an AAV of $17.5 million, the number is lower because he's receiving a lower salary in what would have been his arbitration years. Beginning in 2028, Raleigh will be paid $24.6 million annually.
Will Smith
Will Smith of the Los Angeles Dodgers has the richest catcher contract (by total value). Smith signed a 10-year, $140-million extension with Los Angeles ahead of the 2024 season, buying out his final two arbitration years. However, in typical Dodgers fashion, Smith will be paid $5 million annually from 2034-2043 in deferred payments, lowering the luxury tax hit to just $12 million annually. The deferred payments, expected to be a hot-button topic in ongoing labor talks, paired with Smith being paid through his age-38 season, make the comparison a bit far-fetched.
Before signing the deal, Smith hit .261/.357/.483/.840 with 91 home runs and 306 RBI over five seasons, while providing slightly above-average defense behind the plate.
So... Where does Rutschman fall?
Projecting contracts is an imperfect science. From a strictly production standpoint, Rutschman is most similar to Murphy or Kirk. However, neither player dealt with the same injury problems as Rutschman in the seasons leading up to their extensions. Murphy also represents the closest fit defensively to Rutschman, profiling as one of the best defensive catchers in the sport. The $15 million AAV Murphy would earn from 2025 through 2028 would seem to be the floor of what Rutschman would look for in a potential deal. With MLB Trade Rumors projecting Rutschman to make $9 million in arbitration in 2027, could the Red Sox bump that number up slightly to lower the value of the remainder of the deal to, say, $11 million in 2027 and $14-15 million each year after?
Then, of course, comes the term: catchers especially struggle to cash in on the open market later in their careers. Philadelphia Phillies backstop JT Realmuto posted a line of .257/.315/.384/.700 in 134 games in 2025 before hitting the open market ahead of his age-35 season. Realmuto sat on the free-agent market until Jan. 20, when he signed a three-year, $45-million extension to return to Philadelphia, a move widely criticized as an overpay for a catcher his age.
Red Sox Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow will have to get creative to find common ground with Rutschman. A six-year contract would take him through his age-34 season, having him hit the market at a rather inopportune time. One possible solution for the Red Sox to give Rutschman the long-term commitment he's reportedly seeking could be to front-load the deal, paying him more in his prime while paying him incrementally less as he ages, reducing the franchise's financial burden as he ages and presumably declines.

The 2026 MLB playoffs have arrived!
The 12-team postseason began with an action-packed wild-card round that featured eight teams battling for four spots to advance to the eight-team division series.

item.content:encoded:
How Braves' Ronald Acuna Jr. has impressed analyst despite quiet playoffs showing appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Atlanta Braves won the 2021 World Series without Ronald Acuna Jr., but they are unlikely to go all the way in 2026 unless the franchise pillar comes alive in the playoffs. He was hitting just .167 with a .485 OPS through his last 18 at-bats entering Tuesday's National League Division Series battle versus the Los Angeles Dodgers. One broadcaster is not worried, however.
"He's been okay in the postseason — he hasn't been the superstar yet — but we feel like his moment is coming. Sooner than later," Braves color analyst C.J. Nitkowski told the "Foul Territory" podcast. "The thing I have been impressed with is he's not necessarily become a guy who's pressing. There are times you're watching at-bats and you know he wants to do something big, and you're thinking 'man, he's going to chase here.' And he doesn't.
"He's been under control. It hasn't happened for him just yet… but nobody's worried about the health of Ronald Acuna Jr. {or} his ability to put up big moments here in the postseason."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Ronald Acuña Jr. has wisely avoided pressing in big moments, and it's caught @CJNitkowski's eye…
"He hasn't been the superstar yet, but we feel like his moment is coming sooner rather than later." pic.twitter.com/AJSdOfJVi1
— Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) October 6, 2026
Players live and die by their approach in this sport, and if their process proves successful, the hits will come. The prodigiously talented Acuna believes he will deliver for the Braves when they need him most. Former MVP Award winners tend to be confident, and for good reason. He eventually erupted in the regular season, and fans are trusting him to do the same in October.
Acuna has endured his struggles during this time of the year, however. He owns a .769 OPS through 34 playoff games, which is nearly 130 points lower than his career output. That still might be enough to help Atlanta move forward.
The 28-year-old right fielder is eying his first extra-base hit of the 2026 postseason during a pivotal Game 3 NLDS clash. Ronald Acuna Jr. is still finding ways to contribute, scoring a run in his four previous games, but one big knock could open the flood gates in Truist Park.

item.content:encoded:
The National League’s top-seeded Milwaukee Brewers head to San Diego, California, with a 2-0 lead in their NLDS matchup against the Padres for Game 3 Tuesday night at Petco Park. The Brewers have a chance to advance to the NLCS for the second consecutive year with a win, while the Padres will be fighting to keep their season alive with the help of their home crowd.
The Brewers earned a first-round bye as the No. 1 seed in the NL and home-field advantage throughout the MLB playoffs after finishing the regular season with the best record in the league. While that extra time off during the Wild Card Series has hurt teams with a first-round bye plenty of times in the past, it hasn’t slowed down Milwaukee, which won the first two games of the NLDS against San Diego.
Both games have been one-run contests so far, with Brewers catcher William Contreras playing the hero in Game 1 with his go-ahead solo home run in the seventh inning as Milwaukee went on to win 3-2. The Brewers followed that with a dramatic 4-3 victory in Game 2 when 22-year-old outfielder Jackson Chourio delivered a walk-off two-RBI single against Padres superstar closer Mason Miller.
The Brewers are giving the start to right-hander Dustin May for Game 3. May went 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA across 31 regular season starts between Milwaukee and St. Louis. Tuesday night will be May’s first playoff appearance since he appeared in seven games with the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2020.
The Padres will counter with right-hander Nick Pivetta, who missed a large portion of the season due to injury before making his return on Sept. 7. He posted a 2-0 record with a 1.45 ERA across four starts in September and has pitched really well for San Diego since signing with the team ahead of the 2025 season, owning a 16-7 record with a 2.87 ERA and 0.99 WHIP over the last two regular seasons. Pivetta already made a start for the Padres in the NL Wild Card Series, allowing one run over 3.1 innings against the Chicago Cubs on Sept. 30.
Check out Brewers vs. Padres MLB playoff predictions, picks, and more below ahead of Tuesday night’s NLDS Game 3 at Petco Park.

Brewers vs. Padres MLB Playoff Predictions

Padres vs. Brewers Best Bet: Fernando Tatís Jr. Over 0.5 Runs (-105)
Fernando Tatís Jr. is the tone-setter at the top of the Padres’ lineup, and when a dynamic player like him who’s a major threat on the base paths reaches safely, there’s a good chance he’ll end up coming around to score. Tatís’ 96 runs scored during the regular season were near the top of MLB, and while it’s still a small sample size, his four runs scored during the playoffs so far are tied for the second-most.
Tatís is batting only .176 this postseason, but he has a stolen base and has scored the four runs mentioned above. He scored three runs in the Padres’ Game 1 win over the Cubs in the NL Wild Card Series and then scored a run in Game 2 of the NLDS this past Sunday. item.content:encoded:
Brewers' William Contreras ghosted agent for weeks after Braves trade appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Up 2-0 in their NL Division Series (NLDS) matchup against the San Diego Padres, the Milwaukee Brewers are on the precipice of another NL Championship Series (NLCS) berth. A Game 3 win over the Padres Tuesday night would give the Brewers home-field advantage against the winner of the Los Angeles Dodgers-Atlanta Braves NLDS tilt. On Tuesday, Milwaukee catcher William Contreras appeared on a podcast with former Braves teammate Ronald Acuna Jr. Contreras told his agent to not speak to him for three weeks once the news broke he was heading to Milwaukee, shared by X (formerly Twitter) user Master Flip.
William Contreras stopped talking to his agent for 3 weeks after the Braves traded him to Milwaukee 😳
Acuña: “Did it hurt when you were traded?”
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Contreras: “Of course, bro. I got over it, but when I got here to Milwaukee in 2024, the vibe wasn’t the same, and I was like, damn.… pic.twitter.com/HAv3ZgXINh
— Master Flip | Phillip Feliz 🇩🇴 (@Masterflip_) October 6, 2026
"December 15th, traded to Milwaukee, and it hit," Contreras stated to his former teammate. "I stopped talking to my agent. I told him, don't text me for 3 weeks; I don't want to talk to you. He tells me no, that it's business, and I said that's not business at all. I kept telling him, send me back to Atlanta. I just thought about the guys there because it was a vibe."
As the NL's top seed, there's a good chance that the Brewers could host the Braves in the NLCS. A win on the road Tuesday night would give the Brew Crew some rest before facing off against either prospective opponent. Last year, the Dodgers dispatched the Brewers in a clean sweep. A match against the Braves would likely favor Milwaukee, who is looking to get back to the World Series for the first time since 1982.
In any case, it looks like Contreras is right at home with the Brewers. He's become a multiple-time All-Star and one of baseball's best all-around catchers. Despite a breakout 2022 campaign, the Braves elected to trade for Athletics All-Star Sean Murphy, sending Contreras up north a few days later. Murphy has declined in Atlanta, mostly due to injuries. 2025 NL Rookie of the Year Drake Baldwin has replaced him. Can Contreras lead the Brew Crew back to the Fall Classic? If so, the trade will have paid off quite well in Milwaukee.
Related: Padres go to extreme lengths to mess with Brewers before do-or-die NLDS Game 3

Be sure to join out FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com! Aside from the back-to-back World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers landing back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, the Boston Red Sox made the biggest splash at the trade deadline, landing three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. With only o
item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses the calculus the Red Sox have to make when considering a potential contract extension for All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. Be sure to join out FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
Aside from the back-to-back World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers landing back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, the Boston Red Sox made the biggest splash at the trade deadline, landing three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. With only one season of team control remaining, should the Red Sox extend the 28-year-old backstop?
It took a massive haul of prospects to acquire Rutschman from the division rival Baltimore Orioles, including pitchers Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon, outfielders Enddy Azocar and Harold Rivas, and Carlos Narvaez, Boston's former starting catcher. After being ranked as a top-10 farm system in the sport ahead of the deadline, the Red Sox saw their farm system fall into the bottom 10 as a result of the trade.
Rutschman was a mixed bag in his first two months in a Red Sox uniform, battling both wrist and elbow issues that saw him in and out of the lineup. After hitting just .187/.253/.363/.615 in his first 25 games in Boston, he ended the regular season hitting .333/.355/.567/.922 in the final seven games.
In 32 regular season games, the 28-year-old hit .222/.278/.410/.688 for Boston. Despite the rough numbers, he was one of the few Red Sox players to get a hit during the team's Wild Card series loss to the New York Yankees, going 1-for-8. Given the cost of acquisition, it's safe to say it was an underwhelming outcome for him at the plate.
However, he was incredibly impressive defensively, particularly with the ABS challenge system. In 34 challenges, Rutschman went 24-10, a 71 percent success rate. Every other Boston catcher went a combined 73-48, good for a 60 percent success rate. Rutschman was a noticeable upgrade over Narvaez, who went 32-27, a 54 percent success rate.
While Rutschman was a mixed bag, the prospect haul it took to acquire him all took off after joining their new organization. For Eyanson and Azocar, it was a continuation of breakout seasons that began in Boston. For Witherspoon, it was his first taste of success in professional baseball after struggling in Boston.
Eyanson, the No. 45-rated prospect in baseball, per MLB Pipeline, posted a 2.03 ERA in six starts with Baltimore's Double-A affiliate Chesapeake. He finished the season with a 1.82 ERA over 79 innings across two levels en route to being named a finalist for the Minor League Pitcher of the Year Award, which went to his former LSU teammate, Seattle Mariners starter Kade Anderson.
After hitting .286/.341/.550/.891 with 18 home runs and 27 doubles while driving in 63 runs, while playing excellent outfield defense in 85 games with Single-A Salem and High-A Greenville, Azocar was one of the biggest risers in the Red Sox system in 2026. His breakout season continued in Baltimore, where he hit .327/.372/.529/.901 with three home runs and eight doubles in 25 games for High-A Frederick. After a breakout season, Azocar now ranks No. 99 in MLB Pipeline's top 100 prospects.
It was a rocky first professional season for Witherspoon, the Red Sox first-round selection in the 2025 MLB Draft. The 21-year-old posted a 4.78 ERA in 17 starts with Greenville before being dealt to Baltimore. However, whatever changes the Orioles made seemed to click, as he allowed only two earned runs in his final three starts.
While Rutschman's numbers in his first two months in Boston don't necessarily warrant a long-term extension, giving up such a substantial prospect package to acquire him puts the Red Sox in a bit of a corner.
If the team waits until next season to see how he performs, they risk him not being interested in signing a deal and instead waiting for free agency, where multiple suitors will assuredly be interested. However, he's likely to command a sizable deal even before hitting the open market, one that, at least based on his time in Boston, he hasn't totally earned.
Red Sox Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow was asked about potential extension talks between the two sides in Monday's end-of-season press conference, but he offered a nonanswer and instead praised him for his work with the pitching staff.
"Adley stepped in as our primary catcher in the middle of the season, which is not easy to do, especially when pitching is a strength of our team, and immediately endeared himself to the pitching staff, to the coaching staff, to the clubhouse, just a really, really high-quality teammate and leader," Breslow said. "I think that's something we'll develop internally, and any conversations about what Adley's future will look like will take place between Adley's representatives, Adley, and me," he said about a potential extension.
It'll be an interesting calculus for Breslow to make; the initial deal to acquire Rutschman appears to be a mistake after he underperformed and you once again failed to make a deep playoff run. However, a contract extension could compound that mistake, locking in a player who has failed to stay healthy and underperformed in each of the last two seasons.

item.content:encoded:
By splitting the first two games of the National League Division Series, Atlanta essentially turned a five-game series into a three-game series -- and, oh, by the way, stole home-field advantage from the Dodgers in the process.
Next up, each team will turn to its respective staff ace in a pivotal Game 3 as the series shifts to Truist Park on Tuesday night.
“We know it's two good teams going at it,” Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman said. “We know what's at stake on Tuesday. We need to get that win.”
Just how badly does each team need that win? Consider this: In postseason history, the Game 3 winner in a best-of-five series tied 1-1 has gone on to win the series 48 of 67 times (71.6%).
Here’s everything you need to know ahead of the crucial Game 3:
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 3 is set for 6 p.m. ET/3 p.m. PT on Tuesday at Truist Park. It will be broadcast on FS1/FOX Deportes/FOX One.
All series are available in the US on MLB.TV with authentication to a participating Pay TV provider. Games are also available live internationally, although not in Canada. Sportsnet is MLB's exclusive English-language broadcaster in Canada for every Postseason game, while TVA Sports will be covering the entire AL Postseason and the World Series in French and Broadcaster RDS will cover the entire NL Postseason in French.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Dodgers: RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto   
Key stat: 0.87 WHIP, ranked second among qualified MLB starters
The reigning World Series MVP is set for his 2026 postseason debut with his team looking to reclaim its series lead. Yamamoto could have started Game 1, but the Dodgers liked the way they were lined up for the NLDS and beyond with Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell starting the first two contests. L.A.'s ace is up third as the series shifts to Atlanta, where he gave up one run across 6 1/3 strong innings on Aug. 27; he was outdueled by Sale in a 1-0 loss.
Braves: LHP Chris Sale   
Key stat:  1.96 ERA over his final 24 regular-season starts
Sale will face the Dodgers for the first time since throwing a five-hit shutout against them on Aug. 27. The 37-year-old posted MLB’s third-best ERA (2.16) this year. He began the postseason by limiting the Phillies to three runs over 6 1/3 innings in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series. There was some thought about having him start Game 2, but because he recorded the final four outs of Game 3 of the WC Series, the Braves pushed him back.
What are the starting lineups?
Dodgers: The big change for LA's Game 3 lineup is Shohei Ohtani in the No. 5 spot. Until Tuesday, Ohtani, recovering from right biceps and left knee injuries, had not been fifth or lower in a starting lineup since Sept. 23, 2020. With Sale on the mound, the Dodgers are not only stacking the top half of their lineup mostly with right-handed hitters, they're shaking up their typical starting nine. They already started Miguel Rojas at third base over Max Muncy when facing a lefty opener in Game 2, so it's not a surprise to see Kiké Hernández getting his first start this postseason at the hot corner, shifting Rojas to second.
Braves: Drake Baldwin’s leadoff homer accounted for the game’s only run the last time the Braves faced Yamamoto. Baldwin, Matt Olson and Michael Harris II should all enjoy seeing a right-handed starter. The Braves had faced a lefty starter in four of their first five postseason games. Aaron Nola, the only right-hander they’ve seen, lasted just 1 2/3 innings in Game 3 of the NLWC Series.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Braves: Coming off an off-day, the Braves will have closer Raisel Iglesias and two top setup men, Robert Suarez and Dylan Lee, available. Didier Fuentes and Ray Kerr won’t be available after both threw 40-plus pitches on Sunday.
Dodgers: The bullpen had to cover the final 5 1/3 innings of Game 2 after a shaky start from Snell, but after a series off-day, the Dodgers should have almost everyone available for Game 3. The exception may be Roki Sasaki, who threw two innings on 36 pitches on Sunday.
Any injuries of note?
Dodgers: Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) and Freeman (right knee) are managing lingering injuries. World Series hero Will Klein (right elbow discomfort) has faced hitters, but he has not pitched in a game since July 31 and is viewed as more of a depth option. Blake Treinen (right shoulder inflammation) is unlikely to pitch this postseason.
Who is hot and who is not?
Braves: Harris has two three-hit efforts in five games this postseason and is 8-for-20 (.400) overall. The Braves hope to get Acuña (3-for-18 without an extra-base hit) and Olson (3-for-19 with seven strikeouts) going as the series goes on.
Dodgers: After a tough September, Freeman (3-for-7, home run) swung the bat well in the first two games. Pages (0-for-7) and Tommy Edman (0-for-5) are seeking their first hits this postseason.
Anything else fans might want to know?
- This will be the first time Sale has faced the Dodgers in the postseason since coming out of the Red Sox bullpen to pitch a perfect ninth inning to conclude the 2018 World Series.
- Roberts enters Game 3 one win shy of 71 managerial postseason wins, which would tie Tony La Russa for second-most all-time. Joe Torre holds the record with 84.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Atlanta Braves Announce Strange Ha-Seong Kim News During NLDS vs Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Caleb Kerney
item.description: The Atlanta Braves have an opportunity to break the 1-1 tie and take the lead in their NLDS series against the reigning MLB World Series Champions. Prior to taking on the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Braves announced news about Ha-Seong Kim. Game 3 features a pitching matchup for the ages. item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves have an opportunity to break the 1-1 tie and take the lead in their NLDS series against the reigning MLB World Series Champions. Prior to taking on the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Braves announced news about Ha-Seong Kim.
Game 3 features a pitching matchup for the ages. Chris Sale takes the mound for the Braves, fresh off a 3-2 win that evened the series. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is the starter for the Dodgers.
Game 3 will start at 4:00 PM Mountain Time, 3:00 PM Pacific Time, or 6:00 PM Eastern Time.
Atlanta Braves Announce Ha-Seong Kim & Lane Thomas News Before NLDS Game 3 vs. the Los Angeles Dodgers
Before the first pitch of Game 3 in the NLDS between the Braves and Dodgers, the Braves announced news regarding Kim. This announcement is in regard to his placement in the lineup for the game.
Here is the lineup that the Braves announced prior to the game:
- C: Drake Baldwin
- RF: Ronald Acuna Jr.
- 1B: Matt Olson
- 2B: Ozzie Albies
- CF: Michael Harris II
- LF: Mauricio Dubon
- DH: Sean Murphy
- 3B: Austin Riley
- SS: Ha-Seong Kim
Starting Pitcher: Chris Sale
As you can see, the Braves are going with a near-identical lineup for Game 3. However, the biggest change is pulling Lane Thomas and inserting Kim.
After that, the only other change is moving Dubon from shortstop to LF (to cover the removed Thomas).
Kim is a 30-year-old infielder who played 51 regular-season games. Thomas is a 31-year-old outfielder who came over to the Braves in a trade with the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline.
Reaction To Atlanta Braves Game 3 Lineup
MLB insider Mark Bowman tried to explain today’s lineup decisions.
“Rowdy isn’t in today’s lineup. This weekend, Walt said he likes to have Murphy at DH and Baldwin at C because it allows him to PH for Murph at the right point of a game,” Bowman wrote.
A curious fan brought up an argument, and Bowman responded.
“But why wouldn’t he stack as many LHH as possible in the starting lineup against a tough righty? Could have gone Dubon at SS, Yaz in LF, Tellez at DH…..” the fan wrote.
Bowman replied with some stats regarding Yamamoto: “Yamamoto vs. RHH .586 OPS vs. LHH .510 OPS.”
Looking At Ha-Seong Kim & Lane Thomas
Kim has yet to find success during this postseason run.
Despite playing three games and earning four at-bats, he has yet to record a hit. However, he has recorded a single run, thanks to one of his two walks.
During the regular season, Kim had more offensive success.
In his 51 games, Kim recorded 15 hits, one double, one triple, nine RBIs, 16 walks, and two stolen bases to go along with a .116 batting average.
Thomas, on the other hand, hasn’t experienced much more success than Kim. He has 73 hits, 19 doubles, 40 RBIs, 44 walks, nine stolen bases, and 11 home runs in 118 games.
Additionally, he has a .224 batting average.
It looks like this change could simply be to give Thomas a night off and make sure that Kim gets a game. Because if the Braves were trying to make sure everyone in the lineup could contribute offensively, this is a strange choice.
One way or another, the Braves need to get a win to turn the tides in their favor and take a lead in the series before Game 4.

item.content:encoded:
Ronald Acuña Jr. is one of the most electrifying players in baseball. The Atlanta Braves right fielder is off to a slow start in the playoffs with just three hits in 18 at-bats, but he is capable of changing a game with one swing and the Braves are counting on him to do exactly that.
It is a small sample size. Atlanta has played just five postseason games and is set to take on the Los Angeles Dodgers on Tuesday in Game 3 of the NLDS. The winner puts the other club on the brink of elimination.
Acuña entered the postseason on a tear. In September, the 28-year-old posted a .307 batting average, .347 on-base percentage, .949 OPS, seven home runs and 19 RBIs.
Off the field, Acuña has been busy as well. This year, he debuted his own podcast called La Bestia, interviewing MLB players throughout the season. He recently released an episode in which he announced his plans for the upcoming offseason.
Acuña shared that he plans to work once again with Fernando Tatis Sr., the father of San Diego Padres right fielder Fernando Tatis Jr., this winter.
"I'm going to train throughout the entire offseason with Fernando Tatis Sr. Now that he's in La Guaira, I'm going to head to the stadium every day," Acuña said, via MLB reporter Wilder Sanchez. He added, "The year I won MVP, I trained during the offseason with him."
Ronald Acuña Jr. volverá a trabajar con Fernando Tatis Sr 😱
“La Bestia” tiene como objetivo ganar el MVP en 2027 y repetirá una fórmula que ya le dio resultados en el pasado.
“Voy a practicar durante toda la offseason con Fernando Tatis Sr. Ahora que está en La Guaira voy a… pic.twitter.com/e1jvZZhr8X
— Wilber Sánchez (@wilberdata) October 6, 2026
That year was 2023, when Acuña won the National League MVP unanimously while becoming the first player in MLB history to hit 40 home runs and steal 70 bases in the same season.
Acuña is not in the offseason yet, but he is already making clear that he wants to return to the best version of himself in 2027.
He dealt with a recurring left hamstring strain this year and his overall numbers were not at the level he has set for himself. Going back to the trainer who helped him reach his peak is a smart career move.
For now though, the focus is on the Dodgers. A big Game 3 from Acuña could change the entire series.
Greatest Atlanta Braves of All-Time

item.content:encoded:
Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong wins impressive award ahead of likely MVP appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong is likely going to win the National League MVP Award. Although the Cubs stumbled in the first round of the postseason, PCA turned in an electric regular season. He became the seventh player in MLB history to record a 40/40 season, and Crow-Armstrong achieved many other impressive feats as well. The Cubs star received an award before his expected MVP honor on Tuesday, however. Baseball America named PCA its 2026 MLB Player of the Year.
Cubs centerfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is Baseball America's 2026 MLB Player of the Year ⭐
PCA became the seventh member of the 40 HR / 40 SB club this season, en route to leading MLB in HR (45), R (119) and OPS (1.065).
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
In the 28-year history of BA's MLB Player of the Year… pic.twitter.com/B6hXHhfc9J
— Baseball America (@BaseballAmerica) October 6, 2026
It's not surprising to see Crow-Armstrong land the honor. He does just about everything well on the field.
As mentioned, he had a 40/40 season with 41 stolen bases and a league-leading 45 long balls. Speaking of leading the league, Crow-Armstrong also turned in the best marks in the National League with these statistics: 9.8 WAR (per Baseball Reference), 119 runs scored, .570 slugging percentage, .943 OPS, 156 OPS-plus and 357 total bases.
His Baseball Savant page will make the baseball analytic guys smile to say the least. His offensive rankings are beyond impressive. Meanwhile, he ranked in the 100th percentile for outs above average while playing a premier position in center field. He's also in the 93rd percentile in arm value and 90th percentile in arm strength.
As evidenced by his 41 steals, Crow-Armstrong also runs well. In fact, he's in the 95th percentile for sprint speed.
He's an incredible all-around player. The Cubs' goal is to win the World Series. While they fell short of that feat this year, Chicago will feel confident about its chances of reaching the Fall Classic in the near future with Baseball America's MLB Player of the Year leading the way.

item.content:encoded:
The scenes shift for Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, Oct. 6, and prediction markets offer great trading opportunities.
Unpredictable things happen during the MLB postseason, but if you think you know what will happen, you can stake your claim on Kalshi and Polymarket US.
Aces Chris Sale and Yoshinobu Yamamoto will square off at Atlanta’s Truist Park in a star-studded pitching matchup between the Braves and two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers. The series is even at 1 after Atlanta’s 3-2 win at Dodger Stadium in Game 2.
The Milwaukee Brewers will try to sweep the San Diego Padres in the nightcap at San Diego’s Petco Park.
Let’s look closer at the best sports prediction markets and prices for today’s two games.
Best MLB props for National League Playoffs today
LA Dodgers at Atlanta Braves over/under market
Why Over 6.5 runs could hit
Probability: 51% at Kalshi
Sale and Yamamoto are aces, but these are two of baseball’s most prolific offenses. The Dodgers, of course, have MVPs batting Nos. 1-3 (Mookie Betts, Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman), and Freeman is heating up after an ice-cold September.
Seven runs isn’t a high bar to clear, especially considering Sale’s struggles in October. Sale has a 5.83 ERA in 12 career postseason appearances and allowed three runs to the Phillies in his last postseason start.
The teams totaled eight runs in Game 1, which Dodgers star Tarik Skubal started.
Why Under 6.5 runs could hit
Probability: 49% at ProphetX
These are two of the best pitchers in baseball, and Yamamoto specifically has been a big-game pitcher since he came over from Japan. He was the 2025 World Series MVP. Fewer than seven runs were scored in five of his nine career postseason starts.
Sale has been a bulldog throughout his career, and he’ll need to rise to the occasion to match Yamamoto in an enormous game.
Even though these offenses have elite players, they have not gotten unlocked. Braves star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. has a .485 postseason OPS, and Matt Olsen’s is .543. On the Dodgers’ side, Ohtani, Betts and Will Smith have combined for three hits in 21 at-bats.
Those numbers don’t bode well when facing aces. The first team to two runs may win Game 3.
Milwaukee Brewers at San Diego Padres first five innings market
Why the Padres could win the first five innings
Probability: 47% at Polymarket
The Padres have been striking early throughout the postseason. They have scored first in all four games and have held 2-0 leads in each game in this series.
The Padres have been one of the most dominant teams at home this year, too. They went 51-30 at Petco Park during the regular season and had no trouble rolling the Cubs in the Wild Card round.
Plus, Dustin May is by far the Brewers’ shakiest starting pitcher. He has good career numbers against the Padres (3.14 ERA in 86 innings) but also may be nervous since this will be his first postseason appearance in six years.
Why the Brewers could win the first five innings
Probability: 37% at Kalshi
Milwaukee’s offense has been slow to get going in the series, but it can keep the momentum after its emotional win over the Padres and closer Mason Miller in Game 2.
May may not get more than three innings, but the Brewers bullpen has been awesome, especially in this series. Milwaukee has not allowed any runs in nine innings.
If May can hold down San Diego for one turn through the order, the Brewers can win the first five innings and Game 3.
How prediction markets work for MLB Playoffs trading
All prediction market trades are peer-to-peer, meaning you need a fellow user to buy and sell shares.
Users buy ‘Yes’ and ‘No’ shares on sports results. Each share costs $0.01 to $0.99. All winning shares pay out $1. Losing shares pay out nothing. Low share prices produce bigger payouts.

item.content:encoded:
MLB Best Bets Today October 6
The AL steps aside and the NL takes center stage, as we get Game 3s with a change of scenery in Dodgers vs. Braves and Brewers vs. Padres. After a long day of travel, the teams are back at it, as San Diego looks to stave off elimination and LA and Atlanta are both searching for a huge win to take control of the series. That game has Yoshinobu Yamamoto vs. Chris Sale, while the other game has the potential for all kinds of craziness and lots of bullpen arms. Two very different games to say the least.
Throughout the playoffs, I’ll look at every game on the schedule, even if I don’t have any bets. I’ll typically do this on the morning of the games, trying to achieve as much lead time as possible. Bullpen usage is critically important in the postseason, so I’d be doing a major disservice to do anything before the games are finished and that usually means writing up my thoughts in the morning.
All lines are from DraftKings and are current at the time of publish. Please take the initiative to SHOP AROUND for the best odds. It matters. A lot.
One offering this baseball season is our Opta AI Player Prop Projections. They are for VSiN Pro Subscribers only, so you can check out our current offers here.
Feel free to use my opinions and thoughts, as well as our suite of MLB Betting Tools, including the DraftKings and Circa Betting Splits, Steve Makinen’s Daily Ratings, the 1st 5 Innings Analyzer, and Umpire Stats.
Here are the MLB best bets today for October 6:
Dodgers vs. Braves (-110, 6)
6 p.m. ET
The Dodgers and Braves have flipped back and forth as ever so slight favorites in what is basically a coin-flip affair in Atlanta. The total of 6 definitely illustrates the quality of this pitching matchup, especially because of the caliber of the players in these two lineups. Obviously the Dodgers were among the league’s best and the Braves, while very talented, had a lot of inconsistencies with their hitters.
Sale finished the regular season with a 2.16 ERA, 2.97 xERA, and a 2.29 FIP over his 162.2 innings of work. So far this postseason, he’s pitched 7.2 innings with one start and one relief effort, allowing three runs on five hits with a 12/2 K/BB ratio. Some will probably point to his poor postseason numbers with a 5.83 ERA over 41.2 innings of work, but this is his first time back in the playoffs since 2021, so I’m not really sure any of that matters for what he is now.
LA was fifth in wOBA at .331 against LHP during the regular season, though not all lefties are created equal and not many are Sale. If we start cutting down the sample size, the Dodgers were seventh in wOBA at .329 in the second half against lefties and second with a .366 wOBA in the month of September. But, their 13% BB% is not applicable against a guy like Sale, who throws a lot of strikes.
I’m a bit surprised that the Dodgers didn’t roll with Yamamoto in Game 2, opting instead for Blake Snell. Yamamoto had a 2.53 ERA with a 2.94 xERA and a 3.33 FIP during the regular season over 185 innings. He also would have broken up the run of two straight lefties, but Dave Roberts acknowledged that the Dodgers were thinking about their rotation with the NLCS already, which is pretty presumptuous and was probably some bulletin board material for the Braves.
Yamamoto has already thrown 56 postseason innings with a 2.25 ERA and a 3.45 FIP, as his K% hasn’t been as high, but his BB% has been even better. The Braves were 11th in the league with a .319 wOBA against righties. They were definitely worse against lefties, which perhaps had something to do with Snell being the Game 2 call. The Braves had .316 wOBA against RHP in the second half and had a .317 wOBA against them in September.
Sale has only allowed more than three runs in one start this season, which happened back on April 6. Yamamoto allowed four runs in two of his four September starts. This is a very tight game to say the least. I don’t like a pregame bet in this one. I don’t even have a line on side or total.
Brewers vs. Padres (-138, 7.5)
9:30 p.m. ET
Dustin May and Nick Pivetta are the listed starters here, as this is a much different game than the other one. I’m actually not expecting to see May for very long. I think the right-hander is going to get the team through Fernando Tatis, Manny Machado, and Ty France at least once and maybe try to navigate the bottom of the lineup. My expectation is that we see both Robert Gasser and Shane Drohan. Maybe even Kyle Harrison. There is a lot of data out there about teams hitting relievers better the more that they see them. Those three and Chad Patrick have not pitched yet in this series.
Meanwhile, Trevor Megill, Abner Uribe, and Aaron Ashby have all pitched in both games, while Antonio Senzatela, JoJo Romero, and DL Hall each have one appearance. This will be an all hands on deck approach from Milwaukee and I wouldn’t be surprised if the Padres hitters see a different arm in each plate appearance. May in a short burst sitting 98-99 with movement might fare a bit better than what he usually does.
On the San Diego side, Pivetta really struggled his way through 3.1 innings against the Cubs with four strikeouts and two walks. He only gave up one run on three hits, but it was an arduous appearance. Pivetta only made eight starts during the regular season, with four to start the season and four to finish it. He only allowed 11 runs over 34.2 innings when all was said and done and just three runs in his final four starts.
Joe Musgrove and David Morgan have not pitched in this series yet. Yuki Matsui and Bradgley Rodriguez worked back-to-back days in Games 1 and 2. Mason Miller threw 40 pitches with the loss in Game 2 and Adrian Morejon threw 31 with the loss in Game 1. We could see Walker Buehler here as well as Robbie Ray.
I like the setup better for Milwaukee here with a cavalcade of arms, including several lefties that they can deploy if they wish. I don’t think May will factor into the game as much as the line implies. More specialists for Milwaukee can pitch in the middle innings and guys who can give the Friars a different look. As the underdog price, I think the Brewers are worth a look tonight.
Pick: Brewers +114

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 MLB postseason continues Monday with Game 2 of both American League Division Series. The Chicago White Sox continued their perfect start to the playoffs, winning again over the Cleveland Guardians to take a 2-0 series lead. The White Sox are now 4-0 in the postseason, with all four victories coming on the road.
The New York Yankees, meanwhile, are trying to even their series against the Tampa Bay Rays behind Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler.
Since the best-of-five Division Series became a thing in 1995, the team that won Game 1 has gone on to win the series 73% of the time, and 32% of the time the series ended in a sweep. Winning Game 1 doesn't guarantee a series win, but the White Sox and Rays are in the driver's seat at the moment. Here are the final scores and schedule for Monday's playoff action:
- FINAL: White Sox 4, Guardians 3 (box score); White Sox lead series 2-0
- LIVE: Yankees at Rays (GameTracker); Rays lead series 1-0
To sum up all the ALDS Game 2 action, we're here to declare a winner and loser from both games. You can find those authoritative and inarguable declarations just below.
Winner: The Garrett Crochet trade
For the second time this postseason, the three position players the White Sox received in the Garrett Crochet trade with the Red Sox guided them to a win. , and in Game 2 of the ALDS on Monday. Those three players -- Chase Meidroth, Braden Montgomery, Kyle Teel -- went a combined 4 for 12 with 3 RBI.
Teel helped the White Sox get on the board with his leadoff single in the fourth inning. He later came around to score Chicago's first run on a Munetaka Murakami single. Montgomery provided the game's biggest blow. He drove a two-out, two-run double to right field in the sixth inning, which flipped a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 lead for the White Sox. This, as the kids say, is a nice piece of hitting:
Meidroth followed with a single to right to score Montgomery and give the White Sox what proved to be an important insurance run. The Crochet trade bounty had four of Chicago's six hits in Game 2 and either scored or drove in all four runs. Sean Burke, who was not part of the Crochet trade, threw 5 ⅓ innings of one-run ball behind a pair of openers. He struck out six. He was terrific.
The White Sox did not want to trade Crochet two years ago. They'd just lost a modern record 121 games, however, and needed to add talent up and down the roster. So, Crochet was dealt to Boston, and it sure seems like GM Chris Getz nailed the trade. Three of the four players he received in the deal are playing major roles in October. This is how you draw it up.
are now one win away from their first ALCS since their 2005 World Series win.
Loser: GuardsBall
It is really, really hard to hit in the postseason. Don't believe me? Teams came into Monday hitting .211/.293/.352 this postseason, and .174/.277/.295 in the Division Series. The pitchers are so nasty, they're well-rested thanks to the built-in off-days, and their matchups are all optimized. Every base hit in the postseason is a tiny little miracle, I swear.
The Guardians, two games into their postseason run, are learning that the hard way. They were shut out in Game 1 and held to three hits. In Game 2, they had only four hits, three of which were singles. To date, Cleveland's biggest offensive play in the ALDS is Sean Newcomb's two-run throwing error in the first inning Monday. Here are two of the three runs the Guardians scored in Game 2 (and in the series):
Including Newcomb's error, four of the first five Guardians reached base in Game 2. Only four of the final 30 reached base, most notably Jo Adell's RBI triple in the eighth inning. With all due respect, this is not a dominant White Sox pitching staff. They've had to cobble it together with openers and bullpen games this postseason. Credit to them for keeping Cleveland in check.
The Guardians are not exactly an offensive powerhouse though. They ranked 24th in runs and 27th in home runs during the regular season. It's the same story every year. The Guardians rally in the second half to win the AL Central, then have a hard time putting points on the board in October. That is certainly the case this year. Three runs on seven hits through two ALDS games. Yeesh.
Cleveland is one loss away from elimination. The Guardians are 2-8 in their last 10 postseason games dating back to 2024.

item.content:encoded:
As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention.
This week, all Division Series matchups continue with the White Sox vs. Guardians, Braves vs. Dodgers, Yankees vs. Rays, and Padres vs. Brewers. American League games continue tonight, while National League matchups will pick up tomorrow. Don't want to miss a minute of the action? Here's how you can watch live.
What Time Is the White Sox vs. Guardians Game 2?
Today's game between the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians will take place on Monday, October 5 at 5 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Yankees vs. Rays Game 2?
Today's game between the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays will take place on Monday, October 5 at 8:00 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Braves vs. Dodgers Game 3?
Tomorrow's game between the Atlanta Braves and Los Angeles Dodgers will take place on Tuesday, October 6 at 6 p.m. ET.
What Time Is the Padres vs. Brewers Game 3?
Tomorrow's game between the San Diego Padres and Milwaukee Brewers will take place on Tuesday, October 6 at 9:30 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the MLB Division Series Games
American League Division Series games will be broadcast on TBS, while National League games will be on Fox and FS1. You can also watch them with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fox One, Fubo, HBO Max, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Games For Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to this weekend's games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB Playoffs Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. Things started off with the best-of-three Wild Card Series, where the Braves, Padres, White Sox, and Yankees advanced. Now, the best-of-five Division Series starts October 3. The Cleveland Guardians, Tampa Bay Rays, Los Angeles Dodgers, and Milwaukee Brewers will meet them.
After this round, the Championship Series extends to seven games to determine the best team in each league, who then advance to a best-of-seven World Series. Who will make it all the way?
Chicago White Sox vs. Cleveland Guardians - CWS lead 1-0:
- Game 2 on October 5 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 7 @ 4:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 8 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 10 @ 5:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
Atlanta Braves vs. Los Angeles Dodgers - Series tied 1-1:
- Game 3 on October 6 @ 6:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 4 on October 7 @ 6:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 5 on October 9 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - Fox/Fox One
New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays - TBR lead 1-0:
- Game 2 on October 5 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 7 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 8 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 10 @ 8:00 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
San Diego Padres vs. Milwaukee Brewers - MIL lead 2-0:
- Game 3 on October 6 @ 9:30 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 4 on October 7 @ 10:00 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
- Game 5 on October 9 @ 4:30 p.m. ET - FS1/Fox One
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

item.dc:creator: Matthew Singer
item.description: The Chicago Cubs were swept in the National League Wild Card Series by the San Diego Padres. item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Cubs were swept in the National League Wild Card Series by the San Diego Padres.
While superstar center fielder and X-factor Pete Crow-Armstrong struggled mightily in those two games, going 0-for-7 with four strikeouts, this can't and won't affect his candidacy for regular-season awards.
According to MLB.com, Crow-Armstrong is unsurprisingly a finalist for the Hank Aaron Award. This honor recognizes the most outstanding regular-season offensive performer in each league.
Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani, who is also among this year's finalists, has been honored three consecutive times (one in the American League and two in the National League) and is vying for a fourth.
Will Crow-Armstrong end that streak?
The Case for Chicago Cubs Superstar Crow-Armstrong
Crow-Armstrong was arguably the best player in baseball this season. While the Hank Aaron Award only considers offensive performance, Crow-Armstrong was an elite two-way player.
Crow-Armstrong's stats took a major leap in 2026 after a disappointing second half of the 2025 season. Playing all 162 games, Crow-Armstrong slashed a strong .280/.372/.570 with 45 home runs, 41 stolen bases and 107 runs driven in. He became the seventh member of the vaunted 40-40 club.
He was the engine for this Cubs offense that was one of the best in baseball.
Going beyond just the "basic stats", Crow-Armstrong had a .374 xwOBA, in the 94th percentile among all hitters, according to Baseball Savant. This is a major jump from .321 in 2025. He walked more while increasing his bat speed, as many Cubs hitters did.
While defense isn't part of this award, it's worth noting that Crow-Armstrong had +26 Outs Above Average, the best in baseball among all fielders.
Crow-Armstrong also had a league-leading 9.8 bWAR, just shy of the rare 10.0 bWAR club.
With Ohtani missing time this season, this award is up for grabs this season, despite his finalist nomination. The four-time reigning MVP may have some competition this year.
The Case Against Ohtani
With Ohtani playing 135 games and pitching in just 14, it's quite hard to give Ohtani an MVP or Hank Aaron Award. Ohtani will likely finish second in voting for these two awards, with Crow-Armstrong given an overwhelming 98% chance to win NL MVP over Ohtani, per Kalshi.
The Hank Aaron Award winner almost always reflects the MVP of that league. If Crow-Armstrong is the overwhelming favorite for MVP, he should also be the odds-on favorite for the Hank Aaron Award.
For what it's worth, Ohtani hit 30 home runs with 11 stolen bases and 81 runs driven in, slashing .275/.377/.512 in 2026. These are all career lows since he joined the Los Angeles Dodgers. Ohtani had one of the best runs in MLB history, but it looks like someone else will win MVP in the same league as Ohtani.
After all is said and done, Crow-Armstrong may have some significant hardware at the end of the season. With a likely MVP, Hank Aaron, Gold Glove and Silver Slugger Awards, Crow-Armstrong's trophy case might be getting full soon.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays are back at it Monday night for Game 2 of the ALDS at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida, after an off day Sunday. The Yankees dominated Boston in their AL Wild Card Series to advance to the ALDS to face fellow AL East rivals the Rays, but Game 1 on Saturday was far from how New York performed in the previous round.
The Yankees’ lineup ran into Rays All-Star right-hander Drew Rasmussen in Game 1, who carried a no-hitter into the eighth inning before allowing a double to Austin Wells, who ended up getting thrown out at third base to end the inning while trying to stretch it into a triple. Rasmussen finished his outing with eight scoreless innings and 10 strikeouts, with Bryan Baker recording the save and Jonathan Aranda accounting for the only run of the game with his third-inning solo home run in the Rays’ 1-0 shutout victory.
Veteran right-hander Freddy Peralta will look to shut down New York’s lineup Monday night just as Rasmussen did in Game 1. Peralta had a down year overall, but he ended the regular season strong, posting a 4-0 record with a 0.96 ERA and 0.89 WHIP across five starts in September.
Peralta will be going toe-to-toe with likely 2026 American League Cy Young Award winner Cam Schlittler of the Yankees, who’s set to make his second start of this year’s MLB playoffs. The young right-hander owned a 1.95 ERA and 0.92 WHIP and recorded 239 strikeouts during the regular season. He also pitched 6.1 scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts in a win over Boston in the AL Wild Card Series.
See our Yankees vs. Rays MLB playoff predictions, picks, and more below for Monday night’s ALDS Game 2 at Tropicana Field.
Yankees vs. Rays Odds for Game 2

Yankees vs. Rays MLB Playoff Predictions

The Stats Hub notes that there has been no run scored during the first inning in each of the Yankees’ last six games. That trend could continue Monday night.
There wasn’t much offense at all in Game 1 between the Yankees and Rays on Saturday. The Yankees were shut out and nearly no-hit, and even though the Rays scored a run in the win, Tampa Bay’s offense totaled only five hits and went 0-for-5 with runners in scoring position.
Now Cam Schlittler is taking the mound for the Yankees in Game 2, and we already mentioned how dominant he was during the regular season, in his first start this postseason, and through his first three career playoff outings. We also mentioned that Freddy Peralta didn’t quite have his best season on the mound, but he ended the regular season on a high note and has allowed only three runs over his last six starts.
Both lineups feature plenty of offensive firepower, but it’s hard to ignore how well these two starting pitchers have been throwing the ball.

item.content:encoded:
The Athletic has live coverage of the MLB Playoffs, including the ALDS Game 2s of White Sox vs Guardians and Yankees vs Rays.
After three days of Wild Card Series action, the dust has settled and four teams (Houston Astros, Boston Red Sox, Philadelphia Phillies and Chicago Cubs) have found themselves on an early vacation. Major League Baseball’s 12-team postseason field has been whittled to eight.
Now, the race for the World Series shifts to the next round: the Division Series. Four teams (Cleveland Guardians, Los Angeles Dodgers, Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers) that had first-round byes will now be in action. Additionally, while the Wild Card Series featured a best-of-three format, the Division Series will be best-of-five.
Here’s how MLB’s bracket looks right now:
You can watch the MLB playoffs on Fubo (Stream Free Now).
What is Saturday’s MLB Playoff schedule and starters?
White Sox at Guardians (AL Division Series Game 1): Hagen Smith vs. Parker Messick
First pitch: 1 p.m. ET (TBS)
After the 23-year-old Smith pitched three scoreless innings in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series against the Astros, the White Sox turn to him for an encore performance in Game 1 of the ALDS. While the club was able to pile on six runs against the Astros in a win, it won’t be as easy against the Guardians and Messick.
An All-Star this season, Messick finished his rookie campaign with a 2.56 ERA and 193 strikeouts over 32 starts. Against the White Sox, Messick carded a 2.81 ERA in four starts (25 2/3 innings).
Braves at Dodgers (NL Division Series Game 1): TBD vs. Tarik Skubal
First pitch: 4 p.m. ET (Fox)
Having burned Chris Sale to take Thursday’s winner-take-all game against the Phillies, and with Tyler Mahle also unavailable, the Braves appear to be looking at another bullpen game.
“They’ve pitched in big situations during the season, and no matter who we really see right now in that bullpen in any situation, no matter what inning it is, we’re feeling pretty confident about them,” catcher Drake Baldwin told reporters.
The Dodgers, coming off a first-round bye, will counter with Tarik Skubal, the crown jewel acquisition of this year’s trade deadline. The AL’s reigning Cy Young Award winner has a 2.61 ERA with his new team, his final starts before reaching a highly anticipated free agency.
Yankees at Rays (AL Division Series Game 1): Gerrit Cole vs. Drew Rasmussen
First pitch: 6:30 p.m. ET (TBS)
Faced with an embarrassment of riches on the pitching side, the Yankees will deploy 2023 AL Cy Young Award winner Gerrit Cole against the AL East champs. After Cole in Game 1, the Yankees will have Cam Schlittler in Game 2 and some variation of Max Fried or Carlos Rodón in Games 3 and 4, the last matchup only if necessary.
On the Tampa Bay side, Drew Rasmussen, arguably one of the most underrated aces in the sport, will get the ball at Tropicana Field. For his career, Rasmussen has a 1.81 ERA in 11 games (10 starts) against the Yankees.
Padres at Brewers (NL Division Series Game 1): Robbie Ray vs. Jacob Misiorowski
First pitch: 8:30 p.m. ET (FS1)
Saturday’s final matchup will feature two pitchers at opposite ends of their careers. On the San Diego side, Robbie Ray, the 2021 AL Cy Young Award winner, has been largely unable to replicate the success he had that season. After a deadline trade from the San Francisco Giants to the Padres, Ray has carded a 5.02 ERA over nine starts.
For the Brewers, Jacob Misiorowski is just getting started. An All-Star in his rookie year, Misiorowski finished his sophomore campaign as the favorite to win the NL Cy Young Award, leading MLB with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts. He’s wowed the sport with his ability to repeatedly fire fastballs in excess of 100 mph, and there’s reason to believe that, at 24 years old, his best is yet to come.
What to know about each Division Series matchup
White Sox at Guardians: The two AL Central clubs played each other 13 times during the regular season, with the White Sox winning the season series 7-6. That, however, was not enough to overcome a late surge by the Guardians and a collapse by Chicago that led to the White Sox losing control of the division and having to play their way out of the wild card.
Now, the two clubs will meet again for at least three games, a spot in the Championship Series on the line. By winning the division and finishing with a better record than the AL West winner, the Guardians were granted a first-round bye. No mind, the White Sox dispatched the Astros in two games and have been off since Thursday. That extra rest has allowed the club to realign its depleted pitching staff.
One thing to watch: How Chicago’s thin, matchup-dependent pitching staff is deployed against Cleveland’s newfound offense — the club led the AL in wRC+ (108) from Aug. 1 onward. The urgency, or lack thereof, by White Sox manager Will Venable could swing the series either direction.
Braves at Dodgers: The Braves’ pitching staff will enter Game 1 with very little margin for error, as it will likely be a group effort without a starter available. That alone could be the difference, as teams that take Game 1 in any best-of-five series have historically won the series 72 percent of the time. That said, these Dodgers have not played their best against the Braves, losing the season series 5-1, including a late-August sweep when Tyler Glasnow and Yoshinobu Yamamoto both pitched.
One thing to watch: Shohei Ohtani’s ability to contribute. The four-time MVP has spent much of the second half of the season compromised, leading to an abbreviated September, with some of it on the injured list.
“I do feel like my swing is in a better place, feels smooth, and just a little tweaks here and there, and I’ll be ready for tomorrow,” Ohtani said through interpreter Will Ireton.
Yankees at Rays: Only one team had a better record over its final 30 games than the Rays, who went 20-10 to fend off a late Yankees push to claim the AL East. That, plus a 55-26 home record that tied the Brewers for the best in MLB, has Tampa Bay inching toward its first World Series appearance since 2020. To get there, the Rays will need to beat the Yankees, who made quick work of the Red Sox in the wild-card round. That they did so without Aaron Judge on the roster or needing to call on Giancarlo Stanton in a pinch hit capacity is all the more impressive.
One thing to watch: Junior Caminero was 20 years old the last time the Rays made the postseason, going hitless in two at-bats. Since then, Caminero, now 23, has morphed into a perennial All-Star, hitting 40 home runs in consecutive seasons, the latter of which should earn him major MVP consideration. Few players love the big stage as much as Caminero. One of those players just so happens to be Cam Schlittler, the presumptive AL Cy Young Award winner, who will take the ball at least once this series. How these two match up will be one of the best subplots of this postseason.
Padres at Brewers: In a battle between arguably MLB’s hottest team (the Padres) and the league’s best team all season (the Brewers), there will be a lot of firsts. This is San Diego’s first Division Series under new owners José E. Feliciano and his wife and business partner Kwanza Jones. It will be the first extended runway for Padres rookie catcher Ethan Salas. It will be the first postseason series for Christian Yelich as the Brewers’ captain. And it will be the first time Misiorowski faces these Padres since May.
Should Milwaukee win, it will be the first time in franchise history that the club has made it to back-to-back league championship series. If San Diego upsets MLB’s No. 1 team, it will be the club’s first trip since 2022 and just its fourth overall.
One thing to watch: The bullpens. Behind multiple high-leverage arms, San Diego has made the late innings nearly impossible for opposing teams. If there’s one club that can match the Padres in that regard, it’s the Brewers. The late innings will likely be the deciding factor in who advances.

item.description: Ranking Every MLB Playoff Team's Projected 2026 Postseason Rotation Pitching wins championships.
